parsing_traps.trap: Marketing property-card numbering (1-28) differs from the audited Portfolio Statement numbering (1-27 + held-for-sale). Properties keyed by name, not index.

Optus Centre is the 28th property but is held 49% via a joint venture (equity-accounted) and is NOT in the audited Portfolio Statement. Its valuation (S$251.9m, 49% share) comes from the marketing card (p56); JV carrying value on the balance sheet = S$251,627k.

Two valuation totals exist: audited Portfolio Statement (p162-165) shows S$1,874,519k for the 27 consolidated properties incl. held-for-sale (excludes Optus JV); the marketing portfolio valuation (p43) shows S$2,126,373k incl. the 49% Optus interest. performance.portfolio_value uses the headline S$2,126.4m (incl. proportionate JV) per schema convention.
Financials reported on Group basis (consolidates Australian subsidiaries; JV equity-accounted). Trust-only column ignored.
Income tax is a CREDIT (+S$4.387m) in FY2025, not an expense; stored as income_taxes = -4,387,000 (signed) so net_income = pretax_income - income_taxes holds.

reconciliation.note_gross_revenue: Per-property revenue is disclosed on a GROSS RENTAL INCOME (GRI) basis on the property cards (pp53-57), NOT on the audited Gross Revenue basis. The 27 consolidated properties' GRI sums to ~S$164.7m, which equals the portfolio GRI (excl. the 49% Optus JV). The audited portfolio Gross Revenue is S$186.626m (p158) — higher than GRI because it additionally includes service charges/land rent/property tax recoverables and sale of electricity & RECs. The row-level GRI sum is reconciled here at its own (GRI) basis; it is NOT expected to equal the S$186.6m gross-revenue line, which is a different and broader basis.
reconciliation.line_items_check: Sigma(revenue 186,626) - Sigma(expense 108,817) + Sigma(adjustment -24,355) = 53,454 = net_income (total return after tax, Group)
